allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

title.description: Short human-readable title for the project charter. Use 2–6 words in Title Case, noun phrase identifying the system. Examples: 'Billing Reconciliation API', 'Customer Self-Service Portal', 'Inventory Management Service', 'Checkout Payment Flow'. Anti-patterns: 'Project Charter' (generic placeholder), 'System' (too vague), multi-sentence titles.

problem_statement.description: Concise description of the problem this project aims to solve. Must be at least 20 characters (enforced by minLength). Should identify the affected users/stakeholders, the current pain point, and the business impact. Avoid solution-language; focus on the problem space.

scope_items.description: Single list of the project's scope boundaries: what is delivered now (in), what is deferred (later) and what is excluded (out). At least one item is required (enforced by minItems); there is no per-class floor. Each item states one concrete deliverable, capability, integration, data domain or delivery boundary, and derives from the seed or from a stakeholder need.

items.description: A single scope boundary of the project, carrying its scope class and the links that justify it.

scope_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this scope item. Must be stable across spec versions: links from other nodes reference it. Example: 'scope-jwt-auth'.

text.description: A specific, bounded statement of what this project includes (scope in), defers (later) or excludes (out). Name a concrete capability ('JWT-based authentication for web and mobile clients'), integration ('Stripe payment gateway integration for one-time charges'), data domain ('User profile storage with GDPR-compliant soft-delete') or delivery boundary ('Production deployment to AWS eu-west-1'). Avoid vague items like 'authentication' or 'everything else'. For later and out items, name the specific thing deferred or excluded.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this scope item is derived from (seed documents or stakeholder needs). At least one is required; every scope item must be justified by what it derives from.

scope.description: Whether this scope item is in scope now (in), deferred (later) or excluded (out). later and out require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this scope item is later or out of scope. Required when scope is later or out.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this scope item relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this scope item: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this scope item, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this scope item replaces. Optional.

assumptions.description: Assumptions made during project scoping that could affect delivery if invalidated. At least one must be provided (enforced by minItems). Each should be falsifiable and monitorable.

items.description: A single falsifiable condition taken for granted during project scoping.

assumption_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this assumption. Must be stable across spec versions: links from other nodes reference it. Example: 'asm-legacy-db-unchanged'.

text.description: A specific, falsifiable statement about a condition taken for granted during project scoping. Write in present tense as a fact: 'Existing PostgreSQL user database schema remains unchanged during development', 'Email delivery via SendGrid is available in all target regions', 'Legal review for PII retention policy will complete before beta launch'. Distinguish assumptions from risks: an assumption is something you believe to be true (and must monitor); a risk is something that could go wrong. If an assumption is invalidated during delivery, it becomes a blocking issue.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this assumption is derived from (seed documents). At least one is required; every assumption must be justified by what it derives from.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this assumption: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this assumption, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this assumption replaces. Optional.

risks.description: Known risks that could impact project success or timeline. At least one must be provided (enforced by minItems). Each should be specific enough to have a mitigation strategy.

items.description: A single named risk, carrying its scope class and the links that justify it.

risk_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this risk. Must be stable across spec versions: links from other nodes reference it. Example: 'risk-gateway-instability'.

text.description: A specific, named risk that could impact project success, timeline, or quality. Use concise noun-phrase format: 'Third-party payment gateway API instability during peak load periods', 'Legal review timeline for PII data retention policy exceeds sprint schedule', 'Mobile team dependency on auth service API contract finalisation before Sprint 3'. Distinguish risks from assumptions: a risk is something that might go wrong; an assumption is something believed to be true. Each risk should be specific enough that a mitigation strategy can be written for it.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this risk is derived from (seed documents or charter assumptions). At least one is required; every risk must be justified by what it derives from.

scope.description: Whether this risk is in scope now (in), deferred (later) or excluded (out). later and out require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this risk is later or out of scope. Required when scope is later or out.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this risk relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this risk: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this risk, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this risk replaces. Optional.

stakeholders.description: Array of stakeholder roles and their needs relevant to this project.

items.description: A single stakeholder entry identifying a role and what that role needs from the project.

stakeholder_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this stakeholder. Must be stable across spec versions: links from other nodes reference it. Example: 'sh-product-manager'.

role.description: Functional role describing how this stakeholder relates to this project's outcomes — not their org-chart title or personal name. Decision rule: use the role that captures their accountability to the project deliverables, kept to 2-4 words. Examples: 'Product Manager' (owns feature prioritisation), 'Compliance Officer' (accountable for regulatory sign-off), 'Support Agent' (handles end-user escalations), 'External Auditor' (reviews access and audit logs), 'End User' (primary consumer of the delivered capability). Anti-patterns: 'John Smith' (a name, not a role — names change and cannot be traced to accountability), 'Senior Engineer' (org-chart title that does not describe what this person is accountable for in this project).

needs.description: What this stakeholder needs from the project. Be specific about their measurable success criteria. At least one need per stakeholder (enforced by minItems). Each item names a specific, verifiable outcome and is its own node. Stakeholder needs must be specific enough to inform downstream FRs (Step 04) and NFRs (Step 07) — each need should be traceable to at least one functional requirement or non-functional requirement. Anti-pattern: vague needs like 'good performance' that cannot be mapped to a specific FR or NFR metric.

items.description: A single stakeholder need, as its own graph node.

need_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this stakeholder need. Must be stable across spec versions: links from other nodes reference it. Example: 'need-audit-export'.

text.description: What this stakeholder requires the project to deliver for them to consider it successful. Write as a specific, measurable requirement from their perspective: 'Audit logs retained for 12 months and exportable as CSV for compliance reviews', 'P95 API latency under 200ms so the mobile app meets App Store performance guidelines', 'Role-based access control so support agents cannot view raw payment data'. Avoid vague entries like 'good performance' or 'security requirements' — name the specific outcome this stakeholder needs.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this need is derived from (seed documents). At least one is required; every need must be justified by what it derives from.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this need relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this need: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this need, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this need replaces. Optional.

role_ref.description: Canonical reference to a role defined in the canonical registry. Kind is structurally pinned to role. Example: {"id": "cn:core:role:reviewer", "kind": "role", "label": "Reviewer"}. Omit if no canon entry exists for this role — do not fabricate an ID. Create a canonical_proposals entry instead. Use real example ID: cn:core:role:reviewer

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this stakeholder relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this stakeholder: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this stakeholder, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this stakeholder replaces. Optional.

user_segments.description: Array of distinct user segments the project serves, each with jobs-to-be-done analysis.

items.description: A user segment describing a target audience, their goals, pains, and gains.

segment_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this user segment. Convention: seg-{descriptive-noun}. Examples: 'seg-finance-admin', 'seg-api-integrator', 'seg-self-service-customer', 'seg-support-agent'. Should be stable — downstream nodes (01 capabilities) reference this ID from their derives_from. Anti-pattern: 'seg-1', 'seg-power-user' — sequential labels and generic names cannot be traced to meaning.

description.description: Who this user segment is, characterized by the behavioral, technical, or role-based attributes that make them distinct from other segments. Focus on characteristics that drive different product needs. Examples: 'Finance administrators who reconcile monthly billing across 3+ cost centers using exported CSV reports', 'End customers who view and dispute individual charges via the self-service portal on mobile devices', 'API integrators who embed payment flows into third-party checkout experiences'. Avoid: 'Power users', 'Regular users' — these names do not capture the distinguishing characteristics.

jobs_to_be_done.description: Primary jobs this segment needs to accomplish using this system. Format: imperative verb + specific object + situational context. Examples: 'Reconcile monthly billing charges against internal cost centre codes before the month-end close', 'Dispute a specific charge during an active customer service call without navigating multiple screens', 'Export all transaction history for a given date range as CSV for external audit submission'. Avoid one-word jobs ('Manage orders', 'Process payments') — they omit the context that distinguishes this segment's needs.

pains.description: Current friction points, obstacles, or frustrations this segment experiences without the solution. List the specific mechanism of pain, not just its surface label.

items.description: A specific friction, obstacle, or frustration this segment currently faces. Name the mechanism of pain and its scale or frequency where possible. Examples: 'Manual reconciliation of 3 separate billing systems requiring 4+ hours per billing cycle', 'No visibility into pending charge status until statement closes — every delayed charge triggers a support ticket', 'Cannot export transaction history without contacting support, blocking SOC2 audit preparation'. Avoid surface labels: 'Slow performance', 'Confusing interface', 'Hard to use' — these do not identify the specific friction.

gains.description: Specific, measurable outcomes or benefits this segment expects once the solution exists. Each gain should address one or more of the pains listed above.

items.description: A concrete, measurable benefit this segment will gain from the solution. Include the outcome and an indicator of its scale or value where possible. Examples: 'Reduce monthly billing reconciliation from 4 hours to under 30 minutes by consolidating all billing data in one view', 'See pending charge status in real-time during checkout — eliminates avoidable dispute support tickets', 'Export full transaction history as CSV without human intervention — required for SOC2 audit preparation'. Avoid vague positives: 'Better performance', 'Easier to use', 'Save time' — these do not name the specific outcome or its measure.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this segment is derived from (seed documents). At least one is required; every segment must be justified by what it derives from.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this segment relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this segment: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this segment, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this segment replaces. Optional.

success_metrics.description: Quantifiable metrics used to measure project success. At least 2 must be provided (enforced by minItems).

items.description: A single success metric with target and measurement method, plus optional baseline. When baseline is unknown, omit it rather than guessing — measurement can establish it post-launch.

metric_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this metric. Convention: metric-{noun-phrase}. Examples: 'metric-checkout-conversion', 'metric-api-p95-latency', 'metric-monthly-active-users', 'metric-reconciliation-error-rate'. Must be stable across spec versions — downstream nodes (such as 01 capabilities) reference this ID from their derives_from. Anti-pattern: 'metric-1', 'metric-kpi-3' — sequential labels cannot be traced to meaning.

name.description: Human-readable metric name displayed in reports and dashboards. Use Title Case, 3–6 words, noun phrase describing what is measured. Examples: 'Checkout Page Load Time', 'Monthly Active Users', 'Reconciliation Error Rate', 'API Auth Success Rate', 'Checkout Conversion Rate'. Avoid single words ('Latency', 'Users', 'Errors') — they are ambiguous across multiple metrics. Avoid full sentences or clauses.

baseline.description: Optional. Current measured value before this project begins. If provided, establishes the improvement delta. Include units.

oneOf.description: Current measured value before this project begins, in the same units as the target. When a baseline is unknown, omit the field entirely rather than guessing. Example: if unit is 'ms' and current P95 latency is 450ms, set baseline to 450.

String baseline value when the numeric form is inappropriate. Choose the form based on what you have: (1) numeric when you have a single measured value with units matching the target — e.g., 450 when target is '< 200ms'; (2) string 'unknown' when no prior measurement exists; (3) string 'N/A' when this is a new capability with no prior state; (4) string with range when the current baseline is itself a range — e.g., '4-6 hours per billing cycle'. Use 'unknown' when no current measurement exists yet and a baseline will be established post-launch; 'N/A' when baseline is not applicable because this is a new capability with no prior state; '4-6 hours per billing cycle' when the current baseline is a range with units rather than a single number; '< 5% monthly' when the existing baseline is itself expressed as a threshold. Omit the field entirely rather than guessing. Anti-pattern: '0' as a string when the intent is 'no baseline exists' — use 'unknown' instead, as '0' implies a measured value of zero rather than absence of measurement.

target.description: Measurable target value with units. Decision rule: use the numeric form when the target is a single threshold with no operator (e.g., 200); use the string form when the target needs an operator, condition, or context. Examples: '< 200ms' (string, latency threshold), '>= 99.9%' (string, availability), '< 0.1% error rate' (string, rate), 95 (number, conversion percentage). The string form is preferred — it is self-documenting. Anti-pattern: '200' as a number when the intent is 'under 200ms' — use the string form.

oneOf.description: Use numeric form only when the direction is unambiguous from the metric name. Example: 95 for 'Checkout Conversion Rate' (higher is better, so 95 means 'at least 95%'). Example: 5 for 'Maximum Retry Count' (exact value, not a threshold). If there is any ambiguity about direction or threshold, use the string form instead. Anti-pattern: 200 when the intent is 'under 200ms' — the operator must be explicit, so use the string form '< 200ms'.

Use string form when the target includes an operator (<, >, >=, <=), a unit abbreviation, or a condition expression — this makes the threshold self-documenting. Examples: '< 200ms' (latency threshold with operator and unit), '>= 99.9%' (availability with minimum operator), '< 0.1% error rate' (rate with operator and label). Anti-pattern: writing 200 as a number when the intent is 'under 200ms' — the operator must appear explicitly in the string form.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for this metric. Use standard abbreviations: 'ms' (milliseconds), 'percent' (percentage points), 'count' (raw count), 'req/s' (requests per second), 'MB' (megabytes), 'USD' (currency). The `unit_ref` field links this to the canonical unit registry. Always use the abbreviated form from the approved list: 'ms' (not 'milliseconds'), 'percent' (not 'pct' or '%'), 'count' (not 'number' or 'qty'), 'req/s' (not 'rps' or 'requests per second'). Anti-pattern: 'milliseconds' or 'percentage points' — use the canonical abbreviation so unit_ref can reference the exact term in the canon registry.

measurement_method.description: How this metric is measured. Name the specific tool, dashboard, query, or manual process. Examples: 'P95 latency from DataDog APM dashboard — apm.page.load metric', 'Monthly active users counted from analytics.users_active_monthly BigQuery table', 'Reconciliation error rate from weekly reconciliation job exit code log in CloudWatch'. Avoid: 'Measured by monitoring', 'From the dashboard', 'Manual check' — these are too vague for a reviewer to reproduce the measurement.

unit_ref.description: Canonical reference to the unit defined in the canonical registry. Kind is structurally pinned to 'unit'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:unit:ms", "kind": "unit"} for milliseconds, {"id": "cn:core:unit:percent", "kind": "unit"} for percentages. Must be consistent with the 'unit' field value.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this metric is derived from (seed documents or stakeholder needs). At least one is required; every metric must be justified by what it derives from.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this metric relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this metric: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this metric, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this metric replaces. Optional.

constraints.description: Fixed limits the design must respect (regulation, budget, platform, contractual or organisational constraints). Optional; no minimum number of items.

items.description: A single constraint, carrying its scope class and the links that justify it.

constraint_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this constraint. Must be stable across spec versions: links from other nodes reference it. Example: 'con-eu-data-residency'.

text.description: A specific, verifiable limit the design must respect. Name the source and the boundary: 'Customer data must be stored in EU regions only (GDPR, contract clause 4.2)', 'Total infrastructure spend below 5,000 USD per month', 'Must run on the existing Kubernetes platform, no new runtime'. Avoid preferences ('should be fast') and goals that belong in success metrics.

derives_from.description: Ids of the upstream nodes this constraint is derived from (seed documents or stakeholder needs). At least one is required; every constraint must be justified by what it derives from.

scope.description: Whether this constraint is in scope now (in), deferred (later) or excluded (out). later and out require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this constraint is later or out of scope. Required when scope is later or out.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this constraint relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this constraint: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former or alternative ids of this constraint, kept so that older references still resolve. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this constraint replaces. Optional.
